messages:
mel: quick bring-up thread for op-12b-v1 (open checkpoint). did a baseline fp16 run + int8 and int4 quant experiments. short summary and recs below, pinging @jordan for GTN and @sasha for deploy scheduling.

mel: TL;DR: int8 looks like sweet spot for cost/latency for most product routes. quality drop vs fp16 is small on average but nontrivial on long-context and some reasoning prompts. int4 is attractive cost-wise but has visible regressions on evals -> hold for now. :chart_with_upwards_trend: :money_with_wings:

mel: Setup: 5k eval pairs (mix: 40% chat, 30% summarization, 20% retrieval-aug, 10% arithmetic/logic). 2k long-context tests (>2k tokens). Inference config: greedy+top-p=0.95. Perf on a single A100-like node.

mel: Perf/cost numbers (normalized to fp16=1.0):
- fp16: latency p95=120ms, throughput=250 tok/s, cost=1.00
- int8: latency p95=95ms, throughput=320 tok/s, cost=0.62
- int4: latency p95=88ms, throughput=360 tok/s, cost=0.45

jordan: nice. what's the quality delta on the chat eval? product will want concrete numbers for GTN pricing.

mel: chat pass@1 (overall): fp16=0.78, int8=0.75, int4=0.68.
mel: summarization (ROUGE-L): fp16=0.63, int8=0.61, int4=0.57.
mel: reasoning suite (logic/arithmetic): fp16=0.72, int8=0.66, int4=0.53.

kevin: those reasoning drops look concerning. any specific prompt families that break under int8?

mel: yes — multi-step arithmetic and nested conditionals. Also seen more hallucinations on retrieval-aug prompts when retrieved context is noisy. Long-context (>2k) int8 showed KV-cache drift causing coherence failures in ~0.5% of cases; int4 ~2.8%.

luis: how reproducible noisy cases are — could we detect and route them?

mel: we ran two independent seeds, same patterns. detection looks feasible: a cheap classifier on prompt features + quick proxy rollouts flagged ~70% of failure cases with 1% FP on heldout. So we can route those to fp16.

jordan: for GTN framing: can we say expected unit-cost reduction and expected quality hit if product switches default to int8? need a short blurb + recommended pricing tiers.

mel: recommended wording for GTN: "op-12b-int8: ~38% lower per-token cost than fp16 with <4% average quality regression on chat tasks; recommended as default for read-heavy flows. Provide fp16 fallback for complex reasoning/long-context via classifier-based routing (~2-3% of traffic expected)."

mel: suggested pricing tiers (internal):
- Default (op-12b-int8): baseline price -> 0.62x cost vs fp16.
- Premium (op-12b-fp16): 1.0x price, for high-fidelity routes and SLA.
- Ultra-low (op-12b-int4-beta): offer as experimental opt-in with clear quality caveats (only for short prompts, non-critical tasks).

sasha: operational concerns? can we do canary + auto-fallback if we see quality regressions in prod?

mel: yes — use rollout policies: start 5% traffic on int8, monitor quality metrics (prompt-level surrogate and small reference set), if regressions >2% push to 50% with tighter sampling, else proceed. Auto-fallback hooks available: route to fp16 after N failed proxies or latency anomalies. ci-bot: can create rollout job template.

ci-bot: created canary template: repo redwood/rollouts/op-12b-int8, default 5% -> 25% -> 100% with metrics window 1h.

kevin: what's the recommendation for embeddings / reranking flows? cost-sensitive but quality sensitive too.

mel: embeddings/rerank: int8 is safe for most similarity/rerank where we use representation-based scoring. For final rerank (pairwise LLM scoring) prefer fp16 if budget allows.

jordan: for GTN: propose case study — migration from fp16->int8 for our search product yielded 35% cost reduction with no measurable UX regression in a small pilot. want me to draft a one-pager?

jordan: also question: any license/model-caveats for open checkpoint? legal ok?

mel: ops/research checked license: compatible for hosted usage with attribution requirements; product/legal already signaled OK.

luis: action items?

mel: actions: 1) Sasha schedule canary for next Tue (5% start). 2) CI-bot: attach eval harness with the 5k testset and long-context sampler. 3) Jordan: draft GTN one-pager with the blurb above + pricing tiers. 4) Keven: run focused reasoning stress tests on 10k prompts to validate fallback rate.

mel: final rec: rollout op-12b-int8 as default for cost-sensitive routes, use fp16 fallback for complex prompts, keep int4 in shadow experiments for now. Will post full raw eval CSVs to the eng-ml drive after lunch. :rocket:

jordan: ack, thanks mel :thumbsup:

sasha: ack, will slot canary.

kevin: will run stress tests and share results by EOD Fri.

ci-bot: uploaded eval CSV: s3://redwood-evals/op-12b-v1/1812345678/results.csv
